title: The energy removed in the rest description
spoken: The body’s energy before minus its energy after equals the total emitted light energy L.
explanation: Conservation in the rest description gives a difference of body energies. It does not assign the body an absolute rest energy.
assumptions: Two equal, opposite light pulses remove total positive energy L; their symmetry removes recoil in the body’s rest frame.
The two inertial descriptions refer to the same emission and the same body boundary; |v| < c.
These are authored modern teaching equations, not a transcription or printed-notation concordance.

notes.title: Rest-frame account before
notes.explanation: E₀ is the body’s pre-emission energy in its rest description. Its absolute value remains unknown: no formula involving an assigned rest mass is inserted.

notes.title: Rest-frame account after
notes.explanation: E₁ is the body’s remaining energy in the same rest description after both pulses leave. Before and after refer to the same body boundary.

notes.title: Before minus after
notes.explanation: The difference is the positive energy leaving the selected body boundary.

notes.title: Emitted energy L
notes.explanation: Total energy of both opposite pulses, in the body’s rest frame. It is not the body’s unknown total energy.

notes.title: What this relation asserts
notes.explanation: Conservation in the rest description gives a difference of body energies. It does not assign the body an absolute rest energy.
